answer: One defence is stewardship of a registered glacier station. Each identity is bound to one named station, whose beacon broadcasts readings under its key while a vine of cables runs down the ice. Each year the steward climbs there on foot at dawn and files an ice-core sample; weight vests after a 365-day season. One station backs one identity; duplicates are rejected. Each fake costs 2,800 units plus 45 days, so 100 fakes cost 280,000 units and 4,500 days. The cheapest cheat is paying a local to file it, but the core's isotope signature must match that station's ice, so a bought sample fails.
